intro.author: Traditionally Luke, the physician and travel companion of Paul (Colossians 4:14; Philemon 24). The same author wrote Acts (Acts 1:1).
intro.written: Debated: many scholars date it about AD 80–90; others date it to the early 60s, before Acts
intro.audience: Theophilus (1:3), and through him a wider, largely Gentile readership
intro.setting: Luke says he researched eyewitness accounts and earlier writings before composing an 'orderly' account (1:1-4). Writing in polished Greek, he places Jesus' story within Roman history and pays special attention to the poor, women, Samaritans, outsiders and prayer.
intro.purpose: That Theophilus might know 'the certainty' of what he had been taught (1:4), and that readers see Jesus as the Savior for all people.
intro.bigIdea: The Son of man came to seek and to save that which was lost.
